audience: Inventory and finance users who need to know what the stock on hand is worth, and how that value is calculated.
goal: Read the **stock value** in Odoo: open the **Stock Valuation** report and group it by **Product Category** then **Product**, find out where a product's **cost** is held, see how a **product category** decides the costing method and the valuation account, and read the on-hand **Stock** report grouped by category.
before: You can open the **Inventory** app and its **Reporting**, **Products** and **Configuration** menus.
Your Odoo is set to the company whose stock you want to read. Costing and valuation settings are stored **per company**.
You know which product category you want to check (the guide uses **FG-4W-23**).
outcome: You have read the stock value by category and by product in the Stock Valuation report.
You know where a product's **Cost** is held and which settings value the stock: **Costing Method**, **Inventory Valuation** and **Stock Valuation Account**.
You have read the unit cost and total value in the **Stock** report, grouped by category.
notes: The screenshots were captured by an automated run on a **test database**, in the company **Jinasena (Pvt) Ltd.** The red banner at the top ("Database neutralized for testing") only appears on test databases, and the figures are test data.
This tour is **read-only**. The automated run opens reports, products and categories but changes nothing.

On the test database the **Reporting** menu offers *Stock, Locations, Moves History, Inventory Aging* and *Performance*, but **no Valuation entry**: the menu record has been removed. The automated run therefore opens the same **Stock Valuation** report through its action. On a standard Odoo the entry is **Reporting › Valuation**.
In the Stock Valuation screenshots the only line is **FG-DO-01**: −24 units of one product with a **Total Value of 0.00**. Negative stock has no value, which is why the value is zero.

Product categories are **per company**: two companies can each have a category called FG-4W-23, with different costing settings. The guide's category shows **Average Cost (AVCO)**, **Automated** valuation and the account **ST003 INVENTORY - FINISHED GOODS**.

phases.title: Read the Stock Valuation report
phases.summary: Open the report and group it by category, then product.
phases.checkpoint: You can read the **Total Value** of stock for each category and product.

phases.title: Check a product and its category
phases.summary: See where the cost is held and how the category values stock.
phases.checkpoint: You know the product's **Cost**, and the category's **Costing Method**, **Inventory Valuation** and **Stock Valuation Account**.

phases.title: Read the on-hand Stock report
phases.summary: Group the Stock report by category.
phases.checkpoint: The **Stock** report is grouped by **Product Category**.

glossary.meaning: The accounting value of the stock on hand: quantity multiplied by cost.
The accounting value of the stock for a line, category or product in the Stock Valuation report.
How a product's cost is worked out. **Standard Price** uses the fixed cost on the product, **Average Cost (AVCO)** the weighted average cost, **FIFO** assumes the oldest stock leaves first.
**Manual**: accounting entries for stock are not posted automatically. **Automated**: an entry is created whenever a product enters or leaves the company.
The account that holds the current value of the products of a category when valuation is automated.
The value of one unit of a product, used to value stock when the purchase cost is not known and to compute margins on sales.
A way to collapse a list into groups, for example by category and then by product.

1.title: Open the Reporting menu
1.do: In the Inventory menu bar, click **Reporting**.
actions: Look along the Inventory menu bar.
1.see: A drop-down with the Inventory reports.
1.why: The stock valuation report is under Reporting.
1.tip: If **Valuation** is not in the list (as on the test database), the report can still be opened through its action.

2.title: Open Valuation
2.do: Click **Valuation** to open the **Stock Valuation** report.
actions: Wait for the report to load.
2.see: The **Stock Valuation** report, grouped by **Product**, with columns for quantity, unit value and **Total Value**.
2.why: This report lists every stock movement with its value.
2.warning: On the test database the **Valuation** entry is missing from the menu, so the automated run opens the same report directly.

3.title: Open the search panel
3.do: Click the small arrow at the right of the search box.
actions: Find the small arrow at the right end of the search box.
3.why: You change the filters and the grouping from this panel.

4.title: Switch off grouping by Product
4.see: The **Product** group tag disappears from the search box.
4.why: The report starts grouped by product. You switch that off to start a new grouping.

5.title: Group by Product Category
5.where: Search panel > Group By > Product Category
5.see: The search box now shows **Product Category** and the list is grouped by category.
5.why: It groups the stock value by category.

6.title: Add Product as a second level
6.see: The search box shows **Product Category › Product**.
6.why: You get category first, then product inside each category.

7.title: Expand a category
7.do: Click a category line to open it.
actions: Find a category line, for example **FG-DO-01**.
7.see: The products inside the category appear underneath, with their values.
7.why: Expanding shows which products make up the category's value.
7.tip: Click a product line to expand it further, down to the individual stock movements.

8.title: Read the Total Value column
actions: Find the **Total Value** column (outlined in red).
Read the value for each category and product.
8.see: **Total Value** for each category and product. In the test data it is 0.00 for the only line, because the 24 units are negative stock.
8.why: **Total Value** is the accounting value of the stock.
8.tip: The bottom line is the total for everything in the report.

9.title: Open the Products menu
9.see: A drop-down with **Products** and related entries.
9.why: The product holds its own cost.

10.title: Open Products
10.why: You pick the product whose stock value you want to check.

11.title: Open a product
11.do: Click the product to open it.
actions: Find the product in the list.
11.see: The product form. The test run opens the first product, **C.I. END COVER N110T/1N-Gold Painted**.
11.why: The form shows the product's cost, category and inventory data.

12.title: Read the product's Cost
actions: Find **Cost** on the right of the General Information tab.
12.why: Odoo uses this value to value the product when the purchase cost is not known (for example on an inventory adjustment) and to compute margins on sales orders. With the AVCO costing method it is computed automatically.

13.title: Open the Configuration menu
13.see: A drop-down with the Inventory set-up entries.
13.why: Costing and valuation are set on the product category.

14.title: Open Product Categories
14.why: Every product belongs to a category, and the category decides how its stock is valued.

15.title: Open a product category
15.do: Search for the category and click it to open it.
actions: Type **FG-4W-23** in the search box and press **Enter**.
Click the category in the list.
15.why: The form shows how the category's stock is valued.
15.tip: Categories belong to a company. Open the one of the company you are working in.

16.title: Read the Costing Method
16.where: Category form > Inventory Valuation > Costing Method
points: **Standard Price**: products are valued at the standard cost set on the product.
**Average Cost (AVCO)**: products are valued at the weighted average cost.
**First In First Out (FIFO)**: products are valued assuming that those that enter the company first leave it first.
16.why: The method decides how the cost of a product is worked out.

17.title: Read Inventory Valuation
points: **Manual**: the accounting entries that value the inventory are not posted automatically.
**Automated**: an accounting entry is created automatically when a product enters or leaves the company.
17.why: It decides whether stock movements post accounting entries by themselves.

18.title: Read the Stock Valuation Account
18.where: Category form > Account Stock Properties > Stock Valuation Account
18.see: **ST003 INVENTORY - FINISHED GOODS** in the test data. **Stock Input**, **Stock Output** and **Production** accounts are listed below it.
18.why: When valuation is automated, this account holds the current value of the products of the category.
18.warning: The account fields only appear when **Inventory Valuation** is **Automated**.

19.title: Open the Reporting menu again
19.why: The on-hand **Stock** report also shows the cost and value.

20.title: Open Stock
actions: Wait for the report to load.
20.see: The on-hand report, listing each product with its quantity.
20.why: It shows the stock on hand by product and location, with unit cost and total value.

21.title: Open the search panel
21.do: Click the small arrow at the right of the search box.
actions: Click the small arrow at the right end of the search box.
21.why: You group this report from the same panel.

22.title: Group by Product Category
22.where: Search panel > Group By > Product Category
22.see: The list is grouped by category, each line showing its product count.
22.why: Grouping by category lets you read the unit cost and total value for each category.
22.tip: That completes the tour: stock value by category and product, where the cost is held, how a category values stock, and the on-hand report by category.
